reasoning: Recent data show the 2026 Arkansas Senate race between Republican Sen. Tom Cotton and Democrat Hallie Shoffner is being polled as competitive in at least one Democratic internal poll (R+3), but a newer independent poll and forecasting/prediction sources still indicate a clear Republican advantage, with one poll showing Cotton ahead by 16 points and a forecast describing him as an overwhelming favorite.[1][2][3][4][10] There is no fresh, state-specific general‑election presidential polling in the last 45 days, so the best structural indicator there is Arkansas’s strongly Republican Cook PVI of about R+15, pointing to a substantial but unspecific GOP edge.[15] Overall, synthesizing the July 17–25 Democratic internal poll and the August 18 J.L. Partners survey, plus forecast/prediction commentary, the current evidence supports an Arkansas Senate environment roughly in the R+10–R+15 range, with the more authoritative, non‑campaign polling giving Cotton a double‑digit lead.[2][3][4][10]

sources.name: Hallie Shoffner campaign / 2040 Strategy Group polling memo
sources.details: Campaign-released 2040 Strategy Group poll of 586 likely Arkansas voters found Tom Cotton at 46% and Hallie Shoffner at 43%, an R+3 race within a ±4 point margin of error, described by the campaign as a statistical tie.

sources.name: Arkansas Times summary of 2040 Strategy Group poll
sources.details: Arkansas Times article reports Shoffner campaign’s 2040 Strategy Group poll with Cotton at 46% and Shoffner at 43%, characterizing the race as statistically tied and noting Cotton’s relatively weak favorability.

sources.name: Washington Examiner / J.L. Partners Arkansas Senate poll
sources.details: Washington Examiner reports a J.L. Partners poll of 803 registered Arkansas voters showing Cotton at 51%, Shoffner at 35%, and a Libertarian at 4%, with Cotton leading by R+16 and described as "not in danger" of losing his seat.
sources.date_range: Mid-August 2026 (field dates not specified; article dated August 18, 2026)

sources.name: Octagon Arkansas Senate prediction market/model summary
sources.details: Octagon prediction market and model summary cites the 2040 Strategy Group R+3 poll but states that current polling data indicate an average R+10.2 lead for Cotton (50.3% to 40.1%) and concludes markets and models align that Cotton will win the Arkansas Senate race.

sources.name: ElectionPredictionOfficial Arkansas Senate forecast 2026
sources.details: ElectionPredictionOfficial’s Arkansas Senate forecast describes Tom Cotton as "the overwhelming favorite" in solidly Republican Arkansas, framing the race as strongly tilted toward the GOP without providing a specific numeric margin.

sources.name: KARK coverage of Trump support and past Arkansas presidential results
sources.details: KARK local news piece notes that the Trump/Vance ticket won 64.20% of the Arkansas vote in the 2024 presidential election versus Harris/Walz at 33.56%, while discussing more recent signs of Trump’s support dipping; it does not provide a fresh 2026 state-level general-election margin.

sources.name: Wikipedia summary of Cook Partisan Voting Index for Arkansas
sources.details: Wikipedia’s Cook Partisan Voting Index table lists Arkansas as R+15 statewide, indicating it votes about 15 points more Republican than the national average in recent presidential elections.
